newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan not to scrap state financial institutions.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan not to scrap state financial institutions.

text.p: Pakistan's Finance Ministry said on Sunday that it planned to restructure or merge certain state-owned financial institutions, not to scrap them.

New finance chief Shahid Javed Burki said on Saturday that the government would "abolish, consolidate and reform" the Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan (IDBP), Pakistan Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation (PICIC), Regional Development Finance Corporation (RDFC) and others.
His remarks had caused confusion in the stock market, where financial analysts said they did not fully understand what the new caretaker government led by Meraj Khalid had in mind.

The ministry issued a clarification on Sunday saying that the government was "contemplating the restructuring or merger of institutions like IDPB, RDFC, and possibly some others, with a view to making their operations more effective and commercial".
"Pending the legal and operational steps to be taken in this regard, (the) government of Pakistan will continue to fully support their deposits and operations," the statement said.
It said that the government was not a direct shareholder in PICIC, 55.44 percent of whose equity was in private hands, with the rest held by government-owned corporations.

"The government-owned corporations, like State Life Insurance Corporation, will be asked to consider the possibility of disposing of their holdings in PICIC with the object of making it more efficient and independent," the statement said.

Burki, finance and economic affairs adviser to the prime minister, said in his first news conference on Saturday that the government would scrap the state Pakistan Banking Council and reform several other state-owned financial institutions.

"We are going to abolish the Pakistan Banking Council," said Burki, who took charge of the Finance Ministry on Friday. "We are going to strengthen the supervisory and regulatory authority of the State (central) Bank of Pakistan so that it can better manage, better look after, the banking system."

"(These) institutions serve no purpose at all, have been massively abused in the past, carry enormous amount of burden of bad debts and have to be dealt with very quickly," he said of the loss-making state-run financial concerns.
Analyst Munir Ladha of Karachi-based AKD Securities said the move would help cut down government expenses and prevent these institutions being abused for "political" lending.
"The market hopes that the new economic team will find a suitable way to go about liquidation of these institutions and in the process their investment would remain intact," he said.
Ladha said the market expected the institutions to be merged into a single organisation with prudent lending policies.
